$comment: Site chrome. Build last — these depend on the atoms and on knowing the generated page set.

nav.description: Site header. On restoration and multi-location layouts the nav is doing real conversion work, not just wayfinding.

transparent-overlay.description: Sits over a full-bleed hero, becoming solid on scroll. Used with fullbleed-kinetic heroes.
notes: Scroll state toggles a class at 40px — implemented once as a global behaviour, not per site.
Logo swaps to brand.logoInverse while transparent.

solid.description: Standard opaque header. Supports a mega-menu, which resto-04 and med-02 both need.

centered-logo.description: Logo centred with links either side. Reads as editorial and premium — used by med-01 concierge.

with-cta-bar.description: A thin utility bar above the main row carrying phone, hours or a location switcher. Restoration and multi-location medical default.
notes: The phone number in the utility bar is a tel: link and is the highest-converting element on a restoration site.

responsive.1024: Links collapse into a drawer toggled by a hamburger. The CTA stays visible outside the drawer — burying it costs conversions.
responsive.768: Utility bar reduces to the phone number only.

a11y: Nav wrapped in <nav> with an accessible label.
Mobile toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the toggle on close.
invariants: Never covers content on short viewports — offset by header height, not overlapped.

footer.description: Site footer. On restoration and multi-location layouts this is a primary internal-linking surface, not an afterthought.

minimal.description: Logo, NAP, one row of links, legal. Used where the footer's only job is legitimacy — med-01 concierge.

sitemap.description: Three or four link columns plus NAP. The default.

mega-local.description: Full services × service-areas matrix. Deliberately heavy internal linking — this is what makes the programmatic local pages rank instead of orphaning. Restoration and multi-location medical.
notes: Cap total footer links around 120. Beyond that it stops helping and starts diluting.

responsive.768: Columns stack; the mega matrix becomes collapsible groups rather than an endless list.

a11y: Link text is meaningful on its own — never "click here".
The accessibility statement link is required on every medical build.
invariants: NAP here is byte-identical to the nav, the contact page and the Google Business Profile. qa.mjs checks this.

sticky-mobile-cta.description: A fixed bottom bar on mobile carrying the single most valuable action. Present on every layout in the library because in all three niches the buyer is overwhelmingly on a phone.

showAfter.description: Scroll offset in px before it appears — immediate display competes with the hero CTA.

call-now.description: Restoration. Single full-width tel: button. The highest-converting element on the site.

claim-trial.description: Combat. Free-trial button plus schedule link — the two things a gym visitor is actually looking for.

responsive.base: Rendered below 768px only. Hidden entirely on desktop, where the nav CTA covers this job.

a11y: Body gets bottom padding equal to the bar height so it never covers the footer or the last section.
Real <a>/<button> elements with discernible text — an icon alone is not enough.
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — appears without a slide animation.
invariants: Never overlaps a form field or the footer's legal links.
Tap target is at least 44px tall.
